title: Characteristics of Weather
seo_title: Grade 4 Science: Characteristics of Weather Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Weather is described by temperature, wind, cloud cover and rainfall, measured with instruments such as the thermometer, wind vane, anemometer and rain gauge. Weather data are recorded and interpreted, and PAGASA gives forecasts. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 4, Quarter 4: Earth and Space)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 4: Earth and Space): temperature, wind, clouds and rain, weather instruments, weather data and forecasts. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Weather is described by temperature, wind, clouds and rain.
body_html:
How to think about it

Weather is the condition of the air at a certain time and place. It is described by temperature (hot or cold), wind (speed and direction), clouds and rainfall. Weather can change quickly.

Instruments measure weather: a thermometer measures temperature, a wind vane shows wind direction, an anemometer measures wind speed, and a rain gauge measures rainfall. PAGASA uses weather data to make forecasts.

Example

Which instrument shows wind direction?

An arrow on a pole

Answer: a wind vane

Example

Rainfall over 3 days: 5 mm, 10 mm, 15 mm. Total?

Add

Answer: 30 mm

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the wind vane and the anemometer.
  • Thinking a forecast is always right.
  • Thinking clouds are made of smoke.

items.q: Which agency tells us the weather forecast in the Philippines?
items.e: PAGASA makes daily weather forecasts.

items.q: What weather does this symbol show?
items.e: Weather symbols are on weather forecasts.

items.q: What forms clouds?
c: tiny water droplets made when water vapor cools in the air
items.e: Water vapor condenses into droplets.

items.q: Which tool measures air temperature?
items.e: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

items.q: What causes air masses to move?
c: winds and differences in air pressure
items.e: Air moves from high to low pressure.

items.q: Why do cold fronts often bring thunderstorms?
c: Warm, moist air is pushed up quickly, cools and forms tall clouds.
items.e: Fast-rising air builds storm clouds.

items.q: What is a front?
c: the boundary where two different air masses meet
items.e: Weather often changes at fronts.

items.q: Which tool measures the amount of rain that falls?
items.e: It collects rainwater so it can be measured.

items.q: Which weather is best for drying clothes outside?
items.e: Heat and wind help water evaporate.

items.q: What is an air mass?
c: a huge body of air with about the same temperature and humidity throughout
items.e: Air masses can cover thousands of kilometers.

items.q: Why is it important to know the weather?
c: to plan what to wear and to stay safe
items.e: Weather can affect our activities and safety.

items.q: What does a barometer measure?
items.e: Changes in pressure help forecast weather.

items.q: Which of these describes sunny weather?
c: The sun is shining and the sky is blue.
The grass is white and crunchy in the cold morning.
The sky is gray and covered in clouds, but it is dry.
Water drops fall from the clouds.
items.e: Look and listen to describe the weather.

items.q: After a cold front passes, the weather usually becomes
items.e: Cold, dry air replaces warm, moist air.
